channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Isomorphic Labs in funding talks at a $40B valuation: AI drug design gets a pharma-scale price tag
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Alphabet-backed Isomorphic Labs is in early talks to raise new funding at a valuation of at least $40 billion, Bloomberg reports — potentially $50 billion — just five months after its $2.1 billion Series B. The proposed price tests whether investors believe AI-designed drugs can survive contact with the clinic.

item.title: Confine an AI agent to one folder and one API: hands-on with Strands Box
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Strands Box (strands-agents/box, Apache-2.0) is an open-source sandbox engine for AI agents: operating-system isolation plus deny-by-default policies written in Dogwood. Install it, box the Strands CLI, watch it refuse a file write, then grant exactly that one permission.

item.title: Nuix ships a governed GenAI layer for legal AI: bring your own model, keep the audit trail
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nuix launched the Nuix Neo Generative AI Framework on October 7: a governed orchestration layer that connects a customer's chosen LLM to forensically processed enterprise data — with audit-grade telemetry, policy guardrails, and token metering built for legal, risk, and investigation teams.

item.title: LlamaIndex launches OpenDocRouter: every document model under one API, priced at cost
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: LlamaIndex launched OpenDocRouter on October 7: one API behind 10 document-parsing models — five frontier, five open-source — each benchmarked on ParseBench for quality and cost, with provider token prices passed through at cost.

item.title: Stuut raises $52.5M: AI agents chase the $16 trillion sitting in unpaid invoices
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Stuut announced a $52.5 million Series B led by Insight Partners on October 7, bringing its total funding to $93 million — money to expand the AI agents it says run the entire order-to-cash process for enterprise customers, from missing purchase orders to paid invoices.

item.title: Route tickets, pick tools, and score outputs in 115ms: hands-on with Strands Decider
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Strands Decider (strands-labs/strands-decider, 503 stars, Apache-2.0) is a 1.9B-parameter decision model for agents: it picks between options, answers yes/no, or rates on a scale in about 115 milliseconds — with a calibrated confidence on every answer. Install it, route a support ticket, batch three question types, and serve it over HTTP.

item.title: Preference Model emerges from stealth with a $16M a16z seed — and open-sources Karotte, an RL training framework built to survive cheating models
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Preference Model emerged from stealth on October 7 with a $16 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz, and open-sourced Karotte, the reinforcement-learning environment framework it has been building for frontier labs — hardened through more than a million evaluation runs against models that cheat.

item.title: Microsoft turns agent sandboxing into an OS feature: Execution Containers go GA on Windows 11
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Microsoft made Microsoft Execution Containers generally available on Windows 11 on October 7, turning agent sandboxing from a developer preview into a shipped OS feature. Agents get their own identity, their own sandbox, and their own audit trail — enforced by Windows, not by the app asking nicely.

item.title: Nous Research raises $90M at a $1.5B valuation: the open-source Hermes agent is going enterprise
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nous Research announced on October 7 that it has raised a $90 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, led by Robot Ventures with NVIDIA, Microsoft's M12 and Samsung Next participating. The money will take its open-source Hermes agent into the enterprise — and build a mobile app.

item.title: ChatGPT stops being a text box: GPT-6’s Intelligent UI answers with interactive charts, buttons and mini-apps
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI started rolling out GPT-6 across ChatGPT on October 7 with Intelligent UI, a capability that lets answers arrive as interactive interfaces — charts, buttons, forms and small working tools built on the spot. Paid tiers get it today; free users follow tomorrow.

item.title: Automation Anywhere to acquire Boost.ai: the enterprise AI conversation, from first message to finished back-office work
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Automation Anywhere entered a definitive agreement to acquire enterprise conversational-AI firm Boost.ai from Nordic Capital — its second AI acquisition in a year — betting the next enterprise AI battleground is connecting a customer conversation to the back-office work that resolves it.

item.title: $1.8B to build a virtual cell: Biohub, DOE and NIH commit to the largest AI-ready biology data push ever
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy and the National Institutes of Health announced a combined $1.8 billion commitment to generate the AI-ready biological data needed for predictive models of life — the largest coordinated investment of its kind to date, with Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta adding $300 million more.

item.title: Benchmark how fast your machine really serves AI agents: hands-on with agentperf-local
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: agentperf-local (ArtificialAnalysis/aa-agentperf-local, Apache-2.0) replays real recorded agent conversations against your local model server — llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, LM Studio, or one it starts for you — and reports throughput and latency the way an agent actually experiences them. The full hands-on: install, the 6-turn quick check, the 168-turn comparable run, and the honest trade-offs.

item.title: Google opens the SynthID Detector to everyone: check any image, video or audio for hidden AI watermarks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google's SynthID Detector is now open to everyone, globally: upload any image, video or audio file and check whether it carries an AI watermark from Google, OpenAI, NVIDIA or Kakao. Apple support is coming.

item.title: DeepSights goes everywhere: Market Logic plugs its market-intelligence AI into Copilot, ChatGPT and Claude via MCP
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Berlin's Market Logic Software has made DeepSights MCP generally available: its AI market-intelligence platform now answers inside Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude and Glean, with cited, governed evidence instead of generic model knowledge.

item.title: Tab exits stealth at a $300M valuation: an AI agent that lives in iMessage and books your flights
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: San Francisco startup Tab has emerged from stealth with a $300 million pre-seed valuation, betting the winning personal AI assistant won't be an app at all — it'll be a contact in iMessage and WhatsApp that books flights, calls businesses, and drafts emails.

item.title: Micron's Taiwan workers vote 99% to authorize a strike: they want 15% of the AI memory boom
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Micron’s Taoyuan union said Wednesday that 1,994 members — 99% of those voting — authorized a strike over the bonus scheme, escalating a profit-sharing fight at the memory maker’s largest manufacturing hub, where the DRAM and HBM chips that feed AI servers are made.

item.title: Riverain’s ClearRead chest AI goes enterprise: FDA-cleared lung and heart imaging reaches 2,500 hospitals via RapidAI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Riverain Technologies announced today that its FDA-cleared ClearRead Chest suite will be available through RapidAI’s Rapid Enterprise Platform, putting its lung and cardiac imaging AI in front of radiologists at more than 2,500 hospitals.

item.title: Cut your AI agent's token bill by 20–60%: hands-on with Headroom, the local compression layer
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Headroom (headroomlabs-ai/headroom, ~74.5K stars, Apache-2.0) is a local compression layer for AI agents: it squeezes tool outputs, logs, and JSON before they reach the model — 21–57% fewer input tokens in the project's seeded benchmarks, same answers, nothing leaves your machine. Here is the full hands-on walkthrough, plus the honest trade-offs.

item.title: Atlassian launches AMP: the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol that gives AI agents an identity on your team
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At Team '26 Europe in Amsterdam, Atlassian unveiled AMP — a framework that gives workplace AI agents an assigned identity, scoped authority, shared Teamwork Graph context and reviewable output — alongside a rebuilt Atlassian MCP server with 220+ tools, now generally available.

item.title: Ray Dalio says AI is ‘a classic bubble’ nearing its burst — debt, not the models, sets the clock
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Speaking at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on Wednesday, the Bridgewater founder argued that the AI buildout is increasingly financed with debt, that rising bond yields are raising the cost of data centers and chips, and that “we’re close to” the bursting point — even as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 hit record highs.

item.title: Musk opens Grok Bot to rival models: Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney and Suno will power SpaceX's agent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Elon Musk announced on October 7 that Grok Bot, SpaceX’s persistent AI agent, will route each task to whichever backend model or API performs best — naming rival Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney and Suno. The post passed 3.8 million views, marking a striking multi-model turn for a lab that trains its own frontier models.

item.title: Beyond Now launches an agentic revenue platform for telecoms: native agents that package, sell and bill AI by token and outcome
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Beyond Now launched its Agentic Revenue & Ecosystem Orchestration Platform on October 7, betting that telecoms' AI problem is commercial, not technical: carriers have captured just 2% of AI revenue so far, CEO Angus Ward says, and the missing piece is a revenue stack built for an economy where agents — not humans — do the buying.

item.title: MedScout launches Scout AI: a MedTech rep's whole day done in seconds — and an MCP that plugs its market data into Claude, Copilot, Gemini and ChatGPT
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MedScout launched Scout AI on October 7: an AI that turns its claims-based market data into target lists, meeting briefs and optimized daily routes for MedTech sales reps in seconds — plus a Model Context Protocol server that plugs the same governed data into Claude, Copilot, Gemini and ChatGPT.

item.title: Stop hand-writing agent skills: let Claude Code learn its own — hands-on with AutoHarness
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AutoHarness (tigerless-labs/autoharness, ~9.1K stars, MIT) is a self-learning skill layer for Claude Code: it watches your real sessions, distills the lessons into native skills, merges the near-duplicates, and prunes the ones you never use — no daemon, no benchmark. Here is the full hands-on walkthrough, plus the honest trade-offs.
